title: align stream fragment epochs and stable call handoff for SSE
author: Maya Thompson
description: Motivation: Intermittent corruption was observed when multiple eventstream fragments arrived with overlapping logical epochs, causing partial JSON payloads to be incorrectly attributed to adjacent tool/function-call events. This manifested as truncated toolcall objects and misordered assistant tokens in downstream consumers. This PR introduces an epoch alignment pass in the SSE reassembler, a soft handoff window for function-call sentinels, and heuristics to preserve JSON object boundaries across chunk boundaries. The changes reduce the chance of partial JSON merges and avoid emitting duplicate delimiters when fragments overlap. Summary of changes: 1) Add an epoch-indexed buffer that tags incoming fragments with an epoch token derived from the stream header and sequence offset. 2) Introduce a soft handoff window that delays function/tool-call emission for up to 8ms when an overlapping fragment could contain remaining sentinel bytes. This is a conservative, configurable default to balance latency and correctness. 3) Implement a JSON boundary guard that favors completing a top-level JSON object when the fragment tail suggests a continuation, rather than slicing and emitting an incomplete token. 4) Update the SSE parser unit tests and add an integration scenario that replays interleaved fragments with simulated reorder and partial loss. 5) Add telemetry spans and metrics (sse.epoch_gap_recovered, sse.handoff_delays_ms.histogram, sse.partial_json_rescue) to aid future debugging and rollouts. Backwards compatibility: Default handoff window is small and can be disabled via feature flag sse.handoff.window_ms. No public API changes. Risk: Slight increase in median streaming latency in pathological overlap cases due to the handoff window; metrics are included to monitor impact. Related work: builds on prior fragment-reassembly work in ENG-1987 and complements the partial-json-rescue experiments in ENG-2345. The PR includes a canary rollout plan and escalation steps for reverting the handoff flag if latency regressions exceed thresholds.

ci_details: CI: integration replay harness: passed after re-run
CI: canary evaluator: passed - no perf regression on 10k replayed streams
release_notes: Improve SSE stream resilience by aligning overlapping fragments to logical epochs and introducing a configurable soft handoff window to prevent partial JSON and tool-call truncation. Enable via feature flag sse.handoff.window_ms. Metrics and tracing added to monitor behavior.
canary_plan: Roll out flag to 10% of hosted traffic for 48 hours, monitor sse.partial_json_rescue and sse.handoff_delays_ms.histogram. If partial_json_rescue>0 or error spike resolves while latency increase <5% proceed to 50% and then 100%. Abort and rollback if error rate increases or latency regressions exceed 10% at 10% rollout.
revert_steps: Disable sse.handoff.window_ms flag and redeploy stream reassembler binary. If rollback fails, revert merge commit from main and redeploy previous artifact. Notify SRE and on-call owners listed in docs/rfc/sse-epoch-handoff.md.
notes_for_ops: Feature flag lives in config service under sse.handoff.window_ms. Default 8ms. Dedicated/private customers can set this via operator docs. Telemetry: sse.epoch_gap_recovered, sse.partial_json_rescue, sse.handoff_delays_ms.histogram. Watch dashboards for regressions.
changelog_entry: sse: Add epoch-aligned fragment reassembly and soft handoff to prevent partial JSON and tool-call truncation. Configurable via sse.handoff.window_ms.
